messages:
Omar El-Sayed: Want to lock down a miss-reason taxonomy for KV + prefix cache telemetry before we ship counters everywhere. SRE asked (rightly) that the enum stays stable so dashboards/alerts don’t churn. Proposal below. Please nitpick now.

Omar El-Sayed: Draft miss_reason values (string enum) for `redwood.cache.*.miss_total{miss_reason=...}`:
- `capacity` (no space in cache / evicted due to memory pressure)
- `ttl_expired` (entry existed but expired)
- `policy_disabled` (route or deployment config disabled caching)
- `hash_mismatch` (canonicalization/key mismatch, i.e. prompt differs)
- `version_mismatch` (model version / tokenizer rev mismatch)
- `not_cacheable` (request shape isn’t eligible: e.g. prompt too long / unsupported params)
- `unknown` (fallback bucket; should be rare)

Omar El-Sayed: Notes:
- want same set for prefix + kv even if some are “n/a” so dashboards can compare
- avoid exploding with too many fine-grained reasons; use traces/logs for deep dive

Samir Qureshi: +1 on keeping it small. I’d split `capacity` vs `evicted`? capacity could include “never inserted” cases (prefill too big) vs “was there but got evicted before reuse”. those are different remediation.

Allison Grant: from SRE POV: fewer reasons is better, but they need to map to actions. “capacity” vs “not_cacheable” already covers a lot. If you can’t tell “evicted before reuse” vs “never inserted” reliably, don’t add.

Nadia Rahman: Agree on stable taxonomy. If we add now, it’s hard to remove later because alerts will reference them. Also ingestion rules (cardinality guards) will hardcode allowlist.

Noah Patel: what about `routing_mismatch` / locality? if request got routed to different host/pool than where cache lives, you’ll see misses that look like hash mismatch but aren’t. do we need a reason for “no local cache available”?

Omar El-Sayed: For KV cache specifically we can sometimes attribute to “no KV resident on this replica” but that’s basically capacity/locality. I worry adding `routing_mismatch` is a rabbit hole + not always knowable at runtime.

Julian Moore: scheduler angle: we *can* know when a request didn’t get assigned to the same worker that served prior turn (esp. multi-turn chat). That’s not strictly cache “capacity”. It’s placement.

Caleb Johnson: (telemetry) please keep reasons <= ~8. dashboards will do breakdown pie + time series. also we’re building cardinality budget assuming this set is fixed. adding reasons later ok, but we need process.

Samir Qureshi: Another one: `concurrency_limit`? e.g., if cache lookup is skipped under extreme batching to keep p99? we had that thought in earlier perf discussion.

Omar El-Sayed: If lookup is skipped by policy under load, that’s still `policy_disabled` IMO (just dynamic). but we could add a tag? (probably NO, that’ll explode).

Allison Grant: please no dynamic “load_shed” reason unless you’re 100% sure it’s stable + actionable. We’ll just page on it and hate ourselves.

Nadia Rahman: +1. Also ADR language should match. If we say `policy_disabled` means “didn’t even attempt lookup/insert due to config/policy”, that covers load-shed too.

Noah Patel: on `not_cacheable`: can we define what buckets go in there? prompt too long, streaming? tools? I want to avoid it becoming a junk drawer.

Omar El-Sayed: Yep. Here’s a more explicit mapping (runtime-side, no extra labels):
- `not_cacheable`:
  - prompt tokens exceed max cacheable prefix threshold
  - request has features we don’t cache safely (e.g. non-deterministic sampling config, or unsupported decoding mode)
  - cache key can’t be computed (should be rare)
- `hash_mismatch`: we computed key, looked up, and didn’t find matching entry for that key.

Samir Qureshi: “key can’t be computed” sounds more like `unknown` or `not_cacheable`? but ok.

Caleb Johnson: Please ensure `hash_mismatch` isn’t used for “cache not present on this node”. Those are different stories. Otherwise everyone will chase prompt canonicalization when it’s actually routing.

Julian Moore: can we make `capacity` mean “eligible + attempted lookup but no entry due to eviction/pressure or not resident” (covers routing/locality), and reserve `hash_mismatch` strictly for computed key mismatch? But runtime doesn’t know if miss is due to locality vs eviction.

Omar El-Sayed: For prefix cache we *do* know memory pressure / eviction counters separately. So if miss correlates with eviction pressure, that’s the story.

Allison Grant: +1000. That’s the better path: keep miss reasons simple; rely on eviction pressure + wasted prefill panels to drive triage. Dashboards can overlay.

Nadia Rahman: I’m ok with `capacity` being “eligible + lookup returned miss for non-key reasons (not present / not resident / evicted)”. But then what is `hash_mismatch`? it becomes “eligible + we expected match but key differs”… which is basically normal cold miss too.

Samir Qureshi: careful: a cold miss is just a miss. we can’t know “expected”. `hash_mismatch` in Omar’s list reads like “prompt differs from prior”, but we don’t have a “prior” to compare unless we track session. we’re not doing per-conversation state in metrics.

Omar El-Sayed: good catch. Let me restate:
- For prefix cache, `hash_mismatch` is only when we detect “candidate prefix existed but canonical hash differs” (we have a fast path that checks canonicalized prefix hash for certain routes). If we can’t do that check, we should NOT emit hash_mismatch; it should just be a miss (capacity/unknown).

Noah Patel: that seems too implementation-specific. telemetry taxonomy shouldn’t depend on an optimization.

Allison Grant: agree. if hash_mismatch only fires sometimes, it’s misleading for dashboards.

Caleb Johnson: +1, inconsistent reason coverage is a data quality nightmare. Either it’s universally detectable or don’t include.

Omar El-Sayed: ok. Removing `hash_mismatch` from the stable set. We can still capture canonicalization issues via separate *recommendation logic* later using prompt-length hist + low hit-rate + low eviction pressure patterns.

Samir Qureshi: works for me.

Julian Moore: but we still need something for “version mismatch”, that one is super actionable (rollouts).

Omar El-Sayed: yes keeping `version_mismatch`. That one is detectable reliably (model_version_id / tokenizer_rev in cache key).

Nadia Rahman: Proposed final stable enum (v1):
- `capacity`
- `ttl_expired`
- `policy_disabled`
- `version_mismatch`
- `not_cacheable`
- `unknown`
We can add new reasons only via ADR update + dashboard change window.

Allison Grant: +1. For triage we’ll use:
- miss_total by reason (above)
- eviction_total + pressure gauges
- wasted_prefill_total
Those 3 together answer most “why did cost spike?” questions.

Caleb Johnson: telemetry side: I’ll put these 6 in the ingestion allowlist + drop anything else to `unknown` (or reject). prefer mapping to `unknown` to preserve volume continuity.

Noah Patel: make sure `capacity` doesn’t become “everything”. can we define it in one line in the runtime doc?

Omar El-Sayed: Definition draft:
- `capacity`: cache eligible, lookup attempted, but no reusable entry was found due to non-policy reasons (not present / evicted / not resident). (Eviction/pressure counters provide deeper signal.)
- `ttl_expired`: eligible, lookup attempted, entry found but expired
- `policy_disabled`: lookup/insert skipped by config/policy
- `version_mismatch`: eligible, entry found for same logical key but incompatible version
- `not_cacheable`: request shape not eligible
- `unknown`: fallback

Samir Qureshi: nit: “entry found but expired” vs “not present because expired” might be same in impl. but ok, if you can’t detect reliably, just treat as capacity.

Omar El-Sayed: yep. we’ll only emit ttl_expired where the cache can explicitly report it. otherwise `capacity`.

Allison Grant: Perfect. Please post in the metrics channel + link to whichever ADR captures this so we can reference in runbooks.

Omar El-Sayed: will do. locking v1 as above unless someone screams in next ~24h. :thumbsup:

Nadia Rahman: :thumbsup: I’ll update the metrics naming/cardinality doc to include allowed miss_reason values.

Caleb Johnson: :thumbsup: and I’ll add a guardrail test in ingestion to catch new enums before they hit prod.
